summary: Frontend E2E testing of offline mode (Playwright context.set_offline). Found & fixed 2 bugs in /app/frontend/src/lib/offline.js that broke the core feature: (1) the GET cache stored raw JSON strings (custom adapter runs before transformResponse) so findBase/patchCaches never matched -> no conflict base snapshot (conflict detection NEVER triggered, silent last-write-wins) and offline edits/creations were not reflected in lists; (2) false conflict dialog when editing a sale created offline (base = optimistic item vs server-normalized fields commercial_share/prospecteur_commission). After fixes, all requested flows pass: offline navigation from cache, no logout, banner, offline client note, offline sale edit, offline sale create (+chained edit with temp id remapped), conflict dialog keep-mine and keep-server, regression (online create, prospecteur, carte, 401 redirect).

FIXED BY TESTER: false conflict for PUT on records created offline (temp id offline-*) — dialog showed 'commercial share 1 vs 0.5', 'prospecteur commission — vs 0'
api.get('/clients').then(...) has no .catch -> offline when /clients not cached yet: unhandled 'Network Error' (dev overlay blocks UI) and client PUT silently skipped

Shadcn X close button / Escape do nothing (onOpenChange noop) — confusing; hide close button

Offline saves show 'Vente mise à jour' / 'Vente créée · chantier ajouté au planning' — should say saved locally / pending sync

action_items: Review/keep tester fixes in /app/frontend/src/lib/offline.js (asJson parse in readCache/writeCache; skip conflict check when op.id starts with 'offline-')
Add .catch to api.get('/clients') in EditSaleSheet (and audit other offline-uncached GETs without catch)

On keep-server, still send non-conflicting fields of the op; exclude skipped ops from 'synchronisée' count
Refetch current page data after qylot:synced; fill client_name/author_name in optimistic items
Hide close X in conflict dialog

rca of the issue: axios custom adapter returns the raw XHR response (string body); JSON parsing happens later in transformResponse. writeCache(k, r.data) therefore stored strings; mapArrays/findBase only handle arrays/objects, so base snapshot was always null -> `if (op.base && ...)` never ran conflict detection, and patchCaches never updated lists. Fix: parse strings in readCache/writeCache. Verified conflict dialog then appears with field 'notes' Ma version/Version actuelle and both buttons behave correctly.
